defense_analyst.prose: Pittsburgh leans on the blitz more than on its front four: it sends five or more rushers on 27.1% of dropbacks [dc1] over 362 dropbacks [dc2], 21st in the league [dc3], and averages 4.3 rushers per dropback [dc4]. The payoff is modest: sacks plus QB hits on 14.9% of dropbacks [dc5], 20th in the league [dc6], with a 7.5% sack rate [dc7]. Philadelphia has allowed a 17.2% pressure proxy [dc8] over 355 dropbacks [dc9], so the Eagles' protection holds up reasonably well, but quick game and hot throws are the answer to a blitz-heavy look. Against the run, Pittsburgh averages 6.7 defenders in the box [dc10] over 187 run plays [dc11]. Overall the defense has allowed EPA of -0.01 per play [dc12] over 549 plays [dc13], 10th in the league [dc14], and a 43.5% success rate [dc15]. On third down it allows conversions on 33.9% [dc16] of 112 attempts [dc17], so it is a stop unit that has held up. The red zone is the soft spot: opponents scored touchdowns on 50.0% of trips [dc18], but that rests on only 22 drives [dc19], a small sample. Explosive plays allowed run at 8.6% [dc20], so Philadelphia's chunk plays will have to come from its shot plays against this secondary.

sections.body: Metcalf is the priority: Pittsburgh dropped back on 60.1% of first and second downs [mc1] over 426 plays [mc2], and Metcalf takes 23.6% of targets [mc3] over 297 team targets [mc4]. With Jones and Carter out, coverage needs safety help over the top and no one-on-one shells that let him win the intermediate route. In blitz versus protection, Pittsburgh sends extra rushers on 27.1% of dropbacks [mc5] over 362 dropbacks [mc6], against a 17.2% pressure proxy [mc7] over 355 dropbacks [mc8] allowed by Philadelphia. With DeVonta Smith out after taking 14.4% of targets [mc9], quick game, hot throws and screens to Bernard and Warren become the answer. Pittsburgh's run game is more efficient at 0.09 EPA per run play [mc13] versus -0.07 through the air [mc14], so linebackers must read run first before biting on play fakes. Finally, Pittsburgh's defense has allowed touchdowns on 50.0% of red zone trips [mc15] over 22 drives [mc16], so finishing drives decides the game.
